lines.en: Hi, Luisa! Did you win the chess game yesterday?
lines.pt: Oi, Luisa! Você ganhou a partida de xadrez ontem?

lines.en: No, I lost. The other player was older and more careful than me.

lines.en: Yes, it was longer than the last one. It took two hours.

lines.en: Was it more difficult than the game last week?

lines.en: Yes, it was much harder. I made a bad move at the start.

lines.en: Which piece did you lose first?

lines.pt: Minha rainha. Foi a pior jogada da minha vida.

lines.en: Oh no! A queen is more important than a pawn.
lines.pt: Ai, não! Uma rainha é mais importante do que um peão.

lines.en: I know. Next time I’ll play faster and think better.
lines.pt: Eu sei. Da próxima vez vou jogar mais rápido e pensar melhor.

lines.en: Good plan. Let’s play now. I’m worse than you, so I’ll learn.
lines.pt: Bom plano. Vamos jogar agora. Sou pior do que você, então vou aprender.

facts.big: adjective + er + than · more + adjective + than
facts.label: Comparativos no passado
facts.sub: Compare partidas e pessoas: It was longer than the last one. She was more careful than me. Use good → better e bad → worse.

facts.label: Adjetivos curtos
facts.sub: Com adjetivos curtos, junte er: long → longer, old → older, hard → harder. Depois, use than: It was longer than the last one. Não diga more long.

facts.label: Adjetivos longos
facts.sub: Com adjetivos longos, use more antes: more careful, more difficult, more important. Depois, use than: She was more careful than me.

compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “mais difícil do que”, com mais antes do adjetivo.
compare.tip: Diga: “It was longer than the last one.”
compare.us: Em inglês: adjetivo curto + er (older, longer) ou more + adjetivo longo (more careful). Diga It was harder than the last one.

pages.title: A quiet library · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Saturday morning in a quiet library in Vancouver. A chess board sits on a wooden table. Luisa looks at the black and white squares. Her friend Noel walks in with two coffees. He sits in the chair next to her. He asks about yesterday.
“Hi, Luisa! Did you win the chess game yesterday?” says Noel. “No, I lost. The other player was older and more careful than me.” says Luisa. “Was the game long?” says Noel.
